The problem · in plain words

Rubbish keeps coming back to the same spots, and reports go nowhere

Problem statement

Residents have no simple way to report public rubbish, and today’s channels treat every report as a separate complaint, so the same spots stay dirty.

No clear place to report

Many residents simply give up.

Same pile, many complaints

One problem looks like many.

Nobody knows what’s urgent

Every case waits in the same queue.

Residents never hear back

So next time, they don’t report.

Our survey, n = 44

Our users · 44 residents surveyed, 14–18 November 2026

They care. They just don’t know where to go.

The resident Main user

Walks past the same rubbish on the way to the park or the surau. Doesn’t know which council to call, and if they do report, never hears back.

Needs: one easy way to report, and proof that something happened.

The township manager Decision user

Gets many complaints about the same pile through different channels, with no way to tell which case is urgent.

Needs: one case per spot, ranked by urgency.

“Send reports directly to the correct local council”“Allow follow-up photos if rubbish remains”

The solution · auto simulation

One photo. Five smart steps.

1Report

Snap a photo. The app records the location.

2Verify

AI checks waste type, severity and public land.

3Merge

Same rubbish becomes one hotspot. One confirmation per account.

4Prioritise

3 residents or 3 days unresolved makes it URGENT.

5Track

Residents follow the case to Resolved and earn EcoPoints.

Prototype feedback · what we learned

What worked, what users said, what we’ll change

Hackathon lesson: a working app in one week was not enough on its own. We needed proof from real users, so after the hackathon we surveyed 44 residents.

Tested and working

  • Merging the same rubbish into one hotspot
  • One confirmation per account stops spam
  • Day 2 and Day 3 alerts raise priority
  • EcoPoints and tracking to Resolved

Tested on desktop and iPhone · Flutter + Firebase

What residents said

84.1%

would definitely or probably use SISA

  • Worried about privacy (56.8%) and fake reports (52.3%)
  • Asked to send reports to the correct local council
  • Asked for follow-up photos if rubbish remains

What we’ll change

  • Replace the simulated AI scan with a real image model
  • Route each hotspot to the right local council
  • Add follow-up photos on open cases
  • Review privacy and fake-report checks in a two-week pilot in one residential area
